known_facts_book1: Sits on a three-legged stool in a smoke-filled kitchen nursing a baby, sneezing from the pepper.
Sings a lullaby beginning 'Speak roughly to your little boy, and beat him when he sneezes', shaking the baby at the end of every line.
Says 'Chop off her head!' about Alice in the kitchen, and the cook does not take the hint.
Explains the grinning cat with 'It's a Cheshire cat, and that's why. Pig!'
Flings the baby at Alice and leaves to get ready for croquet with the Queen.
Is under sentence of execution for boxing the Queen's ears, as the White Rabbit tells Alice in a whisper.
Reappears on the croquet-ground in a pleasant temper, tucks her arm into Alice's, and walks off with her.
Has an uncomfortably sharp chin, which she digs into Alice's shoulder.
Finds a moral in everything: 'Everything's got a moral, if only you can find it.'
Turns pale and leaves the instant the Queen appears and says 'Now, I give you fair warning... either you or your head must be off.'
Her cook appears at the trial as a witness, still carrying the pepper-box.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Savage toward her in the kitchen, then relentlessly affectionate and moralising on the croquet-ground; Alice suspects the pepper explains the first.
known_relations_book1.Cheshire Cat: It is her cat, sitting on the hearth and grinning from ear to ear.
known_relations_book1.the Cook: Her cook, who over-peppers the soup, throws fire-irons and saucepans about, and testifies at the trial.
known_relations_book1.Queen: Sentenced her to execution for boxing the royal ears; she flees the croquet-ground at the Queen's warning.
known_relations_book1.White Rabbit: Fears her savage temper and dreads keeping her waiting.

not_in_this_book: the Duchess is the Queen's sister
the Duchess appears in the Looking-Glass world

hallucination_signals: the Duchess's sentence is carried out

known_facts_book1: First seen sitting on the hearth in the Duchess's kitchen, grinning from ear to ear.
Is the Duchess's cat — Alice asks her 'why your cat grins like that?'
Reappears sitting on the bough of a tree, and Alice addresses it as 'Cheshire Puss'.
Tells Alice which way the Hatter and the March Hare live, and that they are both mad.
Says 'we're all mad here. I'm mad. You're mad.'
Vanishes and reappears at will, sometimes very slowly, ending with the grin, which remains some time after the rest of it has gone.
Appears as a head only above the croquet-ground and asks Alice how she is getting on.
Is introduced by Alice to the King as 'a friend of mine'.
The King orders it beheaded, and the executioner argues that you cannot cut off a head where there is no body.
Fades away entirely while the King, the Queen and the executioner are still arguing about it.

known_relations_book1.Alice: The only creature Alice calls a friend; she introduces it to the King and values it as somebody to talk to.
known_relations_book1.Duchess: Its owner — it sits on her kitchen hearth and she explains its grin.
known_relations_book1.King: Objects to the way it looks at him and orders it beheaded.
known_relations_book1.Queen: Wants it executed; the argument over how ends when the head fades away.

not_in_this_book: the Cheshire Cat guides Alice to the Queen's garden
adaptation_inventions: the Cheshire Cat is purple and pink striped

hallucination_signals: the Cheshire Cat is Alice's cat

known_facts_book1: Leans over the fire stirring a large cauldron of soup in the Duchess's kitchen.
Has put far too much pepper in the soup, which is why everyone in the kitchen sneezes.
Throws the fire-irons, then the saucepans, plates and dishes, at the Duchess and the baby.
Does not take the Duchess's hint to chop off Alice's head, and goes on stirring the soup.
Appears at the trial as the second witness, carrying the pepper-box, and says the tarts are made mostly of pepper.
Disappears from the court during the confusion of turning the Dormouse out, before she can be examined further.

known_relations_book1.Duchess: Her cook; pelts her and the baby with kitchenware and testifies at the trial.
known_relations_book1.Alice: No direct exchange; Alice watches her and worries she will act on the Duchess's hint.
known_relations_book1.King: Questions her at the trial and gets 'Pepper, mostly' for an answer.

not_in_this_book: the Cook is a pig or an animal — the text never says what she is

known_facts_book1: There are two of them: a Fish-Footman who delivers the letter, and a Frog-Footman who receives it.
The Fish-Footman produces from under his arm a great letter, nearly as large as himself.
The message is 'For the Duchess. An invitation from the Queen to play croquet', repeated back with the words reordered.
They both bow low and their curls get entangled together.
The Frog-Footman sits on the ground by the door staring stupidly up into the sky and refuses to answer Alice sensibly.
Tells Alice he will sit there 'till tomorrow' and possibly for days.

known_relations_book1.Duchess: Delivers the Queen's croquet invitation to her door.
known_relations_book1.Queen: The invitation the Fish-Footman carries comes from her.
known_relations_book1.Alice: The Frog-Footman answers her questions with maddening literalism and she goes into the house herself.

not_in_this_book: a single Footman — the book has two, a Fish-Footman and a Frog-Footman

hallucination_signals: the Footman opens the door for Alice
